newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler sets 7.1 pct reduction in Q3 output.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler sets 7.1 pct reduction in Q3 output.

text.p: Chrysler Corp said Wednesday it has scheduled production of 585,900 cars and trucks worldwide during the third quarter, down 7.1 percent from the a year earlier due to model changeovers and slower car sales.

Chrysler also said it is reducing its latest second quarter production plan by 7,000 cars from estimates released a month ago. Chrysler now plans to build a total of 711,500 cars and trucks, including 473,500 cars and 238,000 trucks.

In announcing its output plans for the July-September period for the first time, Chrysler, said the 45,100-unit reduction from the 631,000 cars and trucks it built a year earlier was made entirely on the passenger car side.

The automaker plans a major changeover at its Bramalea, Ontario, car plant this summer to prepare it for all-new versions of the Dodge Intrepid, Chrysler Concorde and LHS models, which will cause Canadian car output to drop 59 percent to 21,300 units.
Chrysler also is reducing U.S. car production by 11.2 percent to 104,900 units and Mexican car output by 18.4 percent to 35,300 units, bringing total car output to 155,000 units.
The No. 3 Detroit automaker's U.S. car sales so far this year are down 10 percent to 345,845 units
But Chrysler said it expects third quarter truck production to rise 1.2 percent to 430,900 units from the 425,600 it built a year earlier.
Chrysler will launch production of a new sport utility vehicle, the Dodge Durango, at its Newark, Del., plant this summer.

The third quarter production totals include 20,300 Jeep Grand Cherokees and Voyager minivans that Chrysler plans to build in Graz, Austria, compared to 21,700 produced in the year-ago period. Chrysler plans to build 23,400 vehicles in Graz during the second quarter.
